name: CA-30
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+21 partisan lean in deep-blue Los Angeles County
Incumbent Laura Friedman running with a large financial edge
Republican Scott Meyers raised under $60k with almost no cash on hand
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Friedman: a D+21 district, incumbency, and a fundraising gap of more than 14-to-1, with markets pricing her near-certain. With no contrary polling or ratings, the baseline margin of about 25 points stands.
model.watch: A surprise influx of outside spending against Friedman or an unusually low-turnout special dynamic could narrow the margin, though not enough to threaten the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Laura Friedman, the Democratic incumbent, is heavily favored to win a second full term in this Los Angeles-area seat that leans Democratic by 21 points. She has raised roughly $828,000 and holds nearly $470,000 on hand, while Republican Scott Meyers has raised under $60,000 and reports just a few thousand dollars available. No outside groups are spending against her, and prediction markets give her about a 97% chance of victory.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings exist for the race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and market pricing. The expected margin is about 25 points for Friedman, with the seat rated Safe Democratic.
